_readme: Tenant-portal guided maintenance request. Step 0 is safetyCheck: "I smell gas" and "I see smoke, fire or sparks" are always shown first and skip straight to the safety screen. Then: category -> item -> symptom -> questions (+ assistant tips) -> photos (min 1, required unless the symptom has photosRequired: false) -> review. Priority: collect the priority of every matching rule and answerTip. If any matched, use the highest of those (this lets a Routine rule lower an Urgent basePriority, e.g. heat with the home above 60°F). If none matched, use basePriority. Rank: Routine < Urgent < Emergency. Questions with showIf only appear when that answer is chosen. Emergency screens: flags.gas -> leave home, call 911 and gas company; showFireSafety -> get out, call 911, breaker off if safe; any other Emergency -> call the office now, and the tenant must accept the false-emergency acknowledgment (company setting, SIM REI $100 + vendor emergency charge) before continuing. No acknowledgment for gas or fire. Tenants never pick 'emergency' themselves. Company-specific phone numbers come from settings ({officePhone}).

safetyCheck.shownOn: First screen, above the categories, always visible. Tapping one skips every other step: no questions, no photos, no acknowledgment.

options.label: I smell gas
options.screen: Leave the home now and leave the door open. Don't use light switches, matches or your phone inside. Once you're outside, call 911 and the gas company, then call the office at {officePhone}.

options.label: I see smoke, fire or sparks
options.screen: Get everyone out and call 911. If it's safe and you can reach the breaker panel, turn off the main breaker. Then call the office at {officePhone}.

safetyCheck.afterScreen: Create an Emergency work order right away with whatever the tenant adds (an optional note and optional photos). Page the on-call contact the same way as any other emergency.

symptoms.label: Not cooling or blowing warm air

questions.question: Is the thermostat set to Cool and below the room temperature?
Is the outdoor unit running (fan spinning, humming)?
When was the air filter last changed?
Do you see ice on the copper lines or the indoor unit?
What temperature does the thermostat show inside right now?
Do young children or elderly people live in the home?

tips: Make sure the thermostat is on Cool, set a few degrees below room temperature, and give it 10 minutes.
Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the most common reason an AC stops cooling.
Check the breaker panel for a tripped AC or air handler breaker. Reset it once only.

answerTips.question: filter
answerTips.tip: Your filter may be overdue. If it looks gray or dusty, replace it. A clogged filter can freeze the coil and stop cooling.

answerTips.question: ice
answerTips.tip: Ice means airflow is blocked. Turn cooling OFF and set the fan to ON for about 2 hours to thaw it, then try again.

answerTips.question: tstat
answerTips.tip: Set the thermostat to Cool, a few degrees below room temperature, and wait 10 minutes before submitting.

answerTips.question: out
answerTips.tip: If the outdoor unit isn't running, check the breaker panel and the shutoff box next to the outdoor unit. If a breaker trips again after one reset, leave it off.

rules.tip: It's above 80°F inside, so we're treating this as an emergency. Stay somewhere cool if you can.
With young children or elderly people in the home, we're treating a cooling outage as an emergency.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the thermostat screen and the air filter
symptoms.likelyCause: Clogged filter, frozen coil or a tripped breaker; the technician may also check refrigerant and the capacitor

symptoms.label: Water leaking or dripping

questions.question: Where is the water?
options: Around the indoor unit or closet

questions.question: Is the AC still cooling?
Is there standing water in the pan under the indoor unit?
After turning the AC off at the thermostat, does the water stop within a few minutes?
Is the water reaching a ceiling, another room, or anything electrical?

tips: This is most often a clogged condensate drain line. Algae builds up in the line and water backs up.
Turn the AC off at the thermostat to stop more water from coming out, and put towels down.
If you're comfortable: find the white PVC drain pipe near the indoor unit. If it has a capped T-shaped opening, pour in 1 cup of white vinegar, wait 30 minutes, then pour in a cup of water.
Check outside where the drain pipe ends. If nothing drips out while the AC runs, the line is likely clogged.

answerTips.question: where
answerTips.tip: Water from a ceiling vent can mean the drain pan above the ceiling is overflowing. Keep the AC off and move belongings away from the drip.

answerTips.question: pan
answerTips.tip: A full drain pan points to a clogged drain line. Many units have a safety switch that shuts the AC off when the pan fills.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the water and the indoor unit, including the drain pan if you can see it

symptoms.label: Won't turn on at all

questions.question: Is the thermostat screen on?
Have you checked the breaker panel?
What temperature does the thermostat show inside right now?
Do young children or elderly people live in the home?

tips: Make sure the switch near the indoor unit (it looks like a light switch) is ON.
A full drain pan can trip the safety switch and shut the AC off. If you see water in the pan, go back and choose "Water leaking or dripping."

answerTips.question: screen
answerTips.tip: Replace the thermostat batteries. Most thermostats pull off the wall plate and take 2 AA or AAA batteries.

answerTips.question: brk
answerTips.tip: Reset it once. If it trips again, leave it off. That needs a technician.

answerTips.question: brk
answerTips.tip: Check the breaker panel for the AC and air handler breakers. Reset a tripped one once only.

rules.tip: It's above 80°F inside, so we're treating this as an emergency. Stay somewhere cool if you can.
With young children or elderly people in the home, we're treating a cooling outage as an emergency.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the thermostat and the breaker panel
symptoms.likelyCause: Tripped breaker, dead thermostat batteries, or the safety switch from a full drain pan

symptoms.label: Strange noise or smell

questions.question: What are you noticing?
Turn the system off at the thermostat. Do you see smoke, or is the burning smell still there a few minutes later?

tips: Don't reach inside the indoor or outdoor unit.

answerTips.question: kind
answerTips.tip: Turn the system off at the thermostat and leave it off until a technician checks it.

answerTips.question: kind
answerTips.tip: Squealing or grinding is usually a motor or fan bearing. Turn the AC off to prevent more damage.

answerTips.question: kind
answerTips.tip: A musty smell usually means a dirty filter or standing water in the drain pan. Change the filter if you have one.

answerTips.question: kind
answerTips.tip: Rattling can be a loose panel or debris in the outdoor unit. Turn the AC off if it's loud.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo or short video of the unit making the noise

symptoms.label: Screen blank or not responding
tips: Replace the batteries. Most thermostats pull off the wall plate and take 2 AA or AAA batteries.
Check the breaker for the air handler.
symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the thermostat

symptoms.label: No heat

questions.question: Is the thermostat set to Heat and above the room temperature?
About how cold is it inside right now?

tips: Check the breaker panel for the air handler or heat strip breaker.
A dusty burning smell for the first 30 minutes of the season is normal. A smell that doesn't go away is not.

answerTips.question: mode
answerTips.tip: Switch it to Heat, a few degrees above room temperature, and give it 10 minutes.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the thermostat screen

symptoms.label: Clogged or overflowing

questions.question: Is water overflowing right now?
Turn the valve on the wall behind the toilet clockwise. Did the water stop?
Is this the only toilet in your home?

tips: Don't flush again.
Try a flange plunger (the kind with a rubber sleeve on the bottom) with steady pushes for about 30 seconds.
Please don't use chemical drain cleaners. They can damage the pipes.

answerTips.question: over
answerTips.tip: Turn the valve on the wall behind the toilet clockwise now to stop the water, then put towels down.

answerTips.question: only
answerTips.tip: Since it's your only toilet, we'll treat this as urgent.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the toilet and the floor around it

symptoms.label: Runs constantly
tips: Lift the tank lid and check that the chain on the flapper isn't tangled or too tight.
Jiggle the handle. If the flapper doesn't seal, it usually needs a new one (an inexpensive part).
symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo inside the tank with the lid off

symptoms.label: Leaking at the base
tips: Stop using that toilet if you can, and wipe up the water.
symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the base and the floor
symptoms.likelyCause: Failed wax seal under the toilet

symptoms.label: Clogged or draining slowly

questions.question: Which sink?

tips: Try a sink plunger. In a bathroom sink, cover the overflow hole with a wet cloth first.
Please don't use chemical drain cleaners.

answerTips.question: which
answerTips.tip: If more than one drain is slow, it may be the main line. We'll send a plumber.

answerTips.question: which
answerTips.tip: If the sink has a garbage disposal, run it with cold water first. A jammed disposal often backs up the sink.

answerTips.question: which
answerTips.tip: Pull out the stopper and clean it. Hair builds up there.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the sink with the standing water

symptoms.label: Leaking under the sink

questions.question: When does it drip?
Can you stop the water? Turn the two valves under the sink clockwise.

tips: Turn off the two valves under the sink (clockwise) and put a bowl under the drip.
Move items out of the cabinet so it can dry.

answerTips.question: active
answerTips.tip: A drip only while water runs usually means a drain fitting. Avoid using that sink until it's fixed.

rules.tip: Water that can't be stopped can damage your home and the units around you, so we're treating this as an emergency. Move valuables away from the water and call the office now.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo under the sink showing the pipes and the leak
symptoms.likelyCause: Loose drain fitting or worn supply line

symptoms.label: Faucet dripping
tips: Make sure the handle is turned fully off.
symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the faucet

symptoms.label: Dirty water or sewage coming up

questions.question: Is dirty water or sewage coming up into a tub, shower, or onto the floor?
Is it happening in more than one drain?

tips: Keep children and pets away from any sewage water.

rules.tip: Stop using all water (no flushing, showers, laundry or dishwasher) until a plumber clears the line.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the drain and any water that came up

symptoms.label: No hot water

questions.question: Is your water heater electric or gas?
Is it every faucet or just one?

answerTips.question: type
answerTips.tip: Check the breaker panel for the water heater breaker (usually a double-wide breaker) and reset it once.

answerTips.question: type
answerTips.tip: The pilot light may be out. Don't try to relight it if you smell gas.

answerTips.question: all
answerTips.tip: If only one faucet is cold, the problem is likely that faucet, not the water heater.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the water heater label and the area around it

symptoms.label: Leaking

questions.question: How much water is there?
Turn the cold water valve on top of the heater clockwise. Did the leak stop?

tips: Put towels or a pan down.
If it's leaking heavily, turn the cold water valve on top of the heater clockwise to stop it.
symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the water heater and the water

symptoms.label: Water coming through the ceiling or wall

questions.question: How bad is it?
Is the water near lights, outlets or electronics?

tips: Move belongings away and put a bucket under the drip.

answerTips.question: elec
answerTips.tip: Turn off the breaker for that area and stay away from the water.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the ceiling or wall and anything that's wet

symptoms.label: Not cooling

questions.question: Does the inside light come on?
Is the freezer still cold?

tips: Check the temperature controls: about 37°F for the fridge and 0°F for the freezer.
Make sure food isn't blocking the vents inside.
Check that the doors close and seal all the way around.

answerTips.question: light
answerTips.tip: No light usually means no power. Check that it's plugged in, and check the breaker and any GFCI outlet nearby.

answerTips.question: freezer
answerTips.tip: A cold freezer with a warm fridge often means the vent between them is iced over.

symptoms.photoHint: Take a photo of the inside and the temperature controls
symptoms.likelyCause: Iced-over vent or defrost problem, or a dirty condenser coil

options: From the ice maker or dispenser

questions.question: Can you stop the water? Unplug the fridge or turn off the water line valve behind it.

tips: Wipe up the water so it doesn't damage the floor.

answerTips.question: where

rules.tip: Water that can't be stopped can damage your home and the units around you, so we're treating this as an emergency. Move valuables away from the water and call the office now.

tips: Stop running it and wipe up the water.

rules.tip: Water that can't be stopped can damage your home and the units around you, so we're treating this as an emergency. Move valuables away from the water and call the office now.
